title: Balatro
pros: Endlessly moreish "just one more run" loop
Made by one developer, runs on a toaster
Reinvents poker into something genuinely new
cons: No co-op or multiplayer
Almost no story or narrative hook
Can feel mathematically "solved" once mastered

title: Black Myth: Wukong
pros: Jaw-dropping visuals and boss spectacle
Staff-stance combat is deep and satisfying
A gorgeous take on Journey to the West
cons: No co-op — strictly single-player
Level design can feel linear and invisible-wall heavy
Demanding on GPUs at high settings

title: Hades II
pros: Builds on Hades with more weapons and systems
Melinoë is a strong new protagonist
Signature Supergiant polish even in Early Access
cons: Still Early Access — story is incomplete
No multiplayer of any kind
Balance shifts between updates

title: Warhammer 40K: Space Marine 2
pros: Visceral melee + gunplay against huge Tyranid swarms
3-player co-op campaign and Operations mode
Nails the 40K power fantasy like nothing else
cons: Main campaign is fairly short
PvP mode is thinner than the PvE content
Occasional connection hiccups in co-op

title: Frostpunk 2
pros: Bigger, society-scale scope than the original
Tough political/moral decisions with real weight
Bleak frostpunk atmosphere is unmatched
cons: Faction politics are a steep difficulty spike
Less intimate than the first game for some
Performance dips on large cities

title: Manor Lords
pros: Gorgeous, organic medieval town-building
Deep supply-chain and burgage-plot systems
Enormous solo-dev ambition, actively updated
cons: Early Access — combat and late-game are thin
Steep learning curve with little hand-holding
Content runs dry after the first few hours for some

title: Dragon's Dogma 2
pros: Physics-driven combat and climbable monsters
Pawn system is a clever pseudo-multiplayer twist
Real sense of an untamed, reactive open world
cons: Divisive performance at launch
Fast-travel is deliberately restricted
Story and ending underwhelmed many players

title: Pacific Drive
pros: Your station wagon is a brilliant central "character"
The eerie Pacific-Northwest Zone drips atmosphere
Run-based loop with satisfying upgrade progression
cons: No co-op — solo road trip only
Resource grind can feel repetitive
Crafting and menu UI are a bit clunky

title: Content Warning
pros: Filming monsters for "views" is a hilarious hook
Cheap and perfect for a group games night
Emergent chaos in the Lethal Company vein
cons: Thin without a full group
Content gets repetitive after a few sessions
Not scary or fun solo

title: Satisfactory
pros: First-person factory-building is uniquely immersive
1.0 release added a real ending and progression
Co-op scales to huge collaborative factories
cons: Enormous time sink — "just one more machine"
Combat and exploration are afterthoughts
Optimization headaches can frustrate newcomers

title: Enshrouded
pros: Voxel terrain lets you dig/build almost anywhere
Flying glider + grappling hook make traversal fun early
Frequent, well-received content updates
cons: Still in Early Access — feature/balance changes expected
Base-building tools have a learning curve
Server performance dips with big builds

title: V Rising
pros: Action-combat is sharper than most survival games
Vampire fantasy (shapeshift, blood types) is genuinely unique
PvE-only servers exist if you want to skip PvP
cons: PvP servers can be brutal for casual players
Gearing loop repeats familiar survival-game beats
Castle building is fiddly at first

title: Sons of the Forest
pros: Tense horror atmosphere with genuinely creepy enemies
Building system is more flexible than the original Forest
Companion AI (Kelvin/Virginia) adds character
cons: Story is short relative to genre peers
Enemy AI can feel exploitable once learned
Performance can dip in dense forest areas

title: Palworld
pros: "Pokemon with guns" hook delivered on launch hype
Base-building automation loop is satisfying once it clicks
Sold enormously well — very active playerbase/updates
cons: Still Early Access, content cadence has slowed since launch
Some systems feel derivative of other survival-crafters
Server performance struggles with large bases

title: Helldivers 2
pros: Friendly-fire chaos + big stratagem explosions never get old
Live galactic war gives a reason to keep logging in
Satirical tone is genuinely funny, not just a gimmick
cons: Balance patches have been controversial with the playerbase
Server issues at launch hurt review average
Grind for higher-tier stratagems is noticeable

title: Lies of P
pros: One of the best non-FromSoft soulslikes
Stylish Belle Époque Pinocchio reimagining
Weapon-assembly system rewards experimentation
cons: No co-op
Difficulty spikes hard, especially early bosses
Wears its Bloodborne influence very openly

title: Dave the Diver
pros: Dive-by-day, run-a-sushi-bar-by-night loop is addictive
A constant stream of new minigames and surprises
Charming pixel art and writing
cons: No multiplayer
Jack-of-all-trades — no single deep system
Late-game management can feel like busywork

title: Sea of Stars
pros: Gorgeous modern take on classic SNES-era RPGs
Timed-hit combat keeps battles engaging
Beautiful pixel art and soundtrack
cons: Story is charming but fairly predictable
Local co-op only, no online
On the easy side for genre veterans

title: Baldur's Gate 3
pros: Widely considered one of the best RPGs ever made
Turn-based combat has real tactical depth
Choices meaningfully branch the story across acts
cons: 100+ hour commitment for a full playthrough
Act 3 is notoriously less polished than Acts 1-2
Turn-based combat can feel slow to action-game fans

title: Remnant II
pros: Procedural worlds mean genuine replay variety
Gunplay + Souls-like stamina combat is a rare, well-executed mix
Archetype/class system rewards multiple playthroughs
cons: Difficulty spikes hard against solo players
Some biome/world rolls feel emptier than others
DLC (The Forgotten Kingdom) is priced separately

title: Lethal Company
pros: Best price-to-laughs ratio on this list
Emergent chaos with friends is the entire appeal, and it delivers
Tiny download, runs on almost anything
cons: Not scary or fun solo — needs a group
Content is thin outside the core scavenging loop
Still Early Access, updates can shift balance

title: Cult of the Lamb
pros: Cult-management + roguelike-dungeon blend is unique
Adorably macabre art style
Lots of free post-launch content updates
cons: Cult-sim busywork can grate over time
Combat is simple next to dedicated roguelikes
Co-op was added late and is limited

title: Elden Ring

displayInfo.players: Limited co-op via summon signs (up to 4)

pros: Open-world design gives Soulslike combat room to breathe
Shadow of the Erdtree DLC is one of the best expansions in years
Legendarily deep build variety
cons: Punishing difficulty is a hard wall for some players
Co-op is limited to summon signs, not seamless full-game co-op
No difficulty options — a deliberate but divisive choice

title: Valheim
pros: Gorgeous procedural biomes for a small-studio game
Building system is deep without being fiddly
Cheap and still gets free content updates
cons: Combat feels stiff compared to dedicated action games
Sailing/portal logistics get tedious late-game
No real story beyond boss-hunt structure

title: Icarus
pros: Session/extraction structure is a nice twist on survival-crafting
Talent trees add real build variety
From the DayZ creator — solid engine fundamentals
cons: Mixed-to-fair Steam reviews at points due to bugs and grind
Session timer pressure isn't for everyone
Smaller playerbase than Valheim, matchmaking can be quiet

title: It Takes Two

displayInfo.players: Exactly 2 (split-screen or online), Friend's Pass for one buyer

pros: Constantly reinvents its mechanics — rarely repeats an idea
One person buying gets a free Friend's Pass for the second player
Genuinely moving story about a relationship, not just a gimmick
cons: Requires exactly 2 players — no solo mode at all
One playthrough and you're mostly done
Emotional beats can feel a bit heavy-handed

title: Deep Rock Galactic
pros: Overwhelmingly Positive reviews for a reason — near-perfect co-op loop
Procedural caves keep runs feeling fresh after 100+ hours
Free seasons of new content, no battle-pass pressure
cons: Best played with a full 4-player squad, weaker solo
Class progression grind is real early on
Voice chat/mic culture assumed by the community

title: Hades
pros: Story deepens with every run — rare for a roguelike
Combat feels great from the very first hour
Fully voice-acted cast with genuinely great writing
cons: No co-op or multiplayer of any kind
Isometric hack-and-slash isn't for everyone
Full "true ending" requires a real time commitment

title: Stardew Valley
pros: Made almost entirely solo by one developer — remarkable scope
Extremely relaxing pace, easy to pick up and put down
Regularly gets big free content updates (1.6 and beyond)
cons: Combat/mining is basic and not the main draw
Slow start can feel grindy before systems open up
Co-op has some feature gaps versus solo play

title: Terraria
pros: Absurd amount of content for the price — best $/hour on this list
Still gets free major updates over a decade later
Huge build variety across classes (melee/ranged/magic/summoner)
cons: 2D pixel-art style is a turn-off for some
UI/crafting menus feel dated compared to newer survival games
Progression pacing assumes you look up a wiki eventually

title: Monster Hunter Wilds
pros: Weapon combat is the most fluid the series has been
Seamless open maps with dynamic weather events
Drop-in hunts with friends are effortless to set up
cons: Rough PC performance is the main review complaint
Endgame content thinner than World at launch
Story mode holds your hand far longer than veterans want

title: Hollow Knight: Silksong
pros: Hornet is faster and more aggressive than the Knight
Enormous hand-drawn world with real secrets
Extraordinary value for the asking price
cons: Difficulty spikes hard and early
Sparse in-game direction — expect to get lost
No co-op or assist options of any kind

title: Armored Core VI: Fires of Rubicon
pros: Mech building is deep and genuinely changes how you fight
Boss fights hit as hard as any FromSoftware game
Short missions make it easy to play in bursts
cons: No co-op — PvP is the only multiplayer
Campaign is short compared to their Soulslikes
Assembly menus are intimidating for newcomers

title: Resident Evil 4
pros: One of the best-reviewed remakes ever made
Knife parry system rewards nerve over caution
Runs well across a wide range of hardware
cons: No co-op — strictly single-player
Horror is more action-forward than classic RE
Mercenaries mode is the only real post-game hook

title: Cities: Skylines II
pros: Far deeper economy and road tools than the original
Cities sprawl to a genuinely impressive scale
Heavy mod support through Paradox Mods
cons: Performance problems drove the Mixed review score
Shipped missing features the first game had
Steep learning curve without tutorials

title: Vampire Survivors
pros: Almost certainly the best $/hour on the entire site
Unlock loop is relentlessly moreish
Runs on literally any machine
cons: Intentionally simple — you mostly just move
Screen becomes visual soup at high levels
Co-op is local only, no online

title: Total War: WARHAMMER III
pros: Immortal Empires is a staggeringly large sandbox
Every faction plays genuinely differently
Co-op campaigns with a friend are excellent
cons: Aggressive DLC pricing drags the review score down
Late-game turns get slow on older CPUs
Overwhelming amount of systems for newcomers

title: Age of Empires IV

displayInfo.players: Up to 8 online, co-op vs AI

pros: Asymmetric civilisations keep matchups fresh
Campaign documentaries are a genuinely lovely touch
Still getting substantial free updates
cons: Art style divides long-time Age fans
Ranked ladder can be brutal for beginners
Fewer civs than Age of Empires II after decades of expansions

title: Cyberpunk 2077
pros: Night City is the densest open world on PC
The 2.0 rework fixed the systems people complained about
Branching quests with meaningfully different endings
cons: Still heavy on older GPUs at high settings
No co-op or multiplayer at all
Some launch-era jank survives in side content

title: DOOM Eternal
pros: The best-feeling shooter combat loop on PC
Runs beautifully even on modest hardware
Two large campaign expansions to follow it up
cons: Resource-juggling combat puzzle is not for everyone
Platforming sections divide players
No co-op campaign — PvP only

title: Risk of Rain 2
pros: Item stacking produces absurd, hilarious builds
Escalating difficulty clock creates real tension
Excellent drop-in co-op with friends
cons: Later DLC had a rocky reception
Can feel repetitive solo
Little in the way of story or direction

title: Factorio
pros: The gold standard for automation games
Famously never goes on sale — but never needs to
Mod scene is enormous and well supported
cons: Genuinely addictive in a way that eats weekends
Top-down 2D art undersells the depth
Combat is the least interesting system

title: Outer Wilds
pros: One of the best-designed mysteries in any game
Knowledge, not gear, is the only progression
The ending lands like nothing else on this list
cons: Almost no replay value once you know the answers
Zero-g flying takes real practice
Time loop pressure frustrates some players

title: Phasmophobia
pros: Voice recognition means ghosts hear what you actually say
Terrifying with friends, genuinely tense solo
Still getting free content years into Early Access
cons: Still Early Access with rough edges
Investigation loop repeats once you learn the ghosts
Best experience needs voice chat and ideally VR

title: Red Dead Redemption 2
pros: Arguably the finest story and cast in any open world
Detail density that still has not been matched
Enormous amount of content for one purchase
cons: Deliberately slow, weighty movement frustrates some
Red Dead Online is effectively abandoned
Very large install and demanding at high settings

title: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
pros: Deflection combat is the sharpest FromSoftware has written
Sengoku Japan setting is gorgeous and distinct
Grappling hook makes traversal genuinely fun
cons: No summons or co-op — you beat the bosses alone
Almost no build variety to fall back on
Hardest entry point of any FromSoftware game

title: Slay the Spire
pros: The game that defined the roguelike deckbuilder genre
Four characters with completely different deck identities
Ascension levels give hundreds of hours of difficulty
cons: No multiplayer of any kind
Presentation is plain next to newer deckbuilders
Run losses can hinge on bad card draws

title: Disco Elysium - The Final Cut
pros: Some of the best writing in the medium, full stop
Your skills argue with you as separate characters
Fully voiced in the Final Cut at no extra cost
cons: Zero combat — it is a reading game
Dense prose is a real time investment
Studio turmoil means no sequel is coming

title: Monster Hunter: World
pros: Still the best-value entry point to the series
Fourteen weapon types that play like different games
Iceborne expansion nearly doubles the content
cons: Menus and crafting systems are labyrinthine
Multiplayer session flow is famously clunky
Frequently discounted — rarely worth full price

title: Celeste
pros: Tight controls that make failure feel fair every time
Handles anxiety and self-doubt with real care
Assist mode makes it accessible without judgement
cons: Genuinely demanding platforming in later chapters
Short main story if you skip B-sides
No multiplayer at all

title: Dead Cells
pros: Combat feels razor-sharp and responsive
Years of free updates on top of paid DLC
Boss Cell difficulty tiers give it a long tail
cons: No co-op or multiplayer
Weapon RNG can stall a promising run
DLC is priced steeply relative to the base game

title: RimWorld
pros: The AI storyteller generates disasters you will retell for years
Mod ecosystem is one of the largest on Steam
Effectively unlimited replayability
cons: Sparse visuals hide a very deep game
No co-op — colony management is solo
Expansions add up in cost

title: Subnautica
pros: Ocean exploration nothing else has matched
Genuine sense of dread without being a horror game
Base building and story pull in the same direction
cons: No co-op in the base game
Thalassophobia makes it unplayable for some
Little reason to replay once the map is known

title: Hollow Knight
pros: Outstanding value — huge world for the price
Hallownest is atmospheric and quietly devastating
Four free content expansions post-launch
cons: Deliberately vague about where to go next
No map until you find the cartographer each area
Late-game challenges are punishing

title: Dark Souls III

displayInfo.players: Co-op via summon signs (up to 3 phantoms)

pros: The most refined and approachable of the Dark Souls trilogy
Boss design is consistently excellent
Summon co-op still has an active playerbase
cons: Co-op is limited and fiddly to set up
Level design is more linear than Dark Souls I
PvP invasions can be unwelcome

title: Sid Meier's Civilization VI
pros: The definitive "one more turn" game
District system gives cities real spatial planning
Deeply discounted bundles appear constantly
cons: Base game is thin — the expansions are close to mandatory
Late-game turns drag badly
AI struggles at higher difficulties without bonuses

title: Don't Starve Together
pros: Distinctive Tim Burton-ish art that has aged perfectly
Still receiving free content a decade on
Cheap, and often bundled two-for-one to gift a friend
cons: Brutally unforgiving without a wiki open
Permadeath frustrates a lot of new players
Character unlocks take a long grind

title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
pros: Side quests written better than most games' main stories
Two enormous expansions included in most editions
Free next-gen update keeps it looking modern
cons: Combat is the weakest part of the package
Inventory and menus feel dated
Slow opening few hours before it opens up

title: Project Zomboid
pros: The most detailed zombie survival sim on PC
Every death writes a story worth telling
Huge mod scene and active multiplayer servers
cons: Still Early Access after more than a decade
Isometric presentation hides a steep learning curve
You will die a lot before you understand why

title: Portal 2
pros: Still one of the funniest games ever written
The 2-player co-op campaign is entirely separate content
Runs on anything and costs almost nothing
cons: Short, and puzzles rarely surprise on a replay
Co-op needs a committed partner to finish
No new Valve follow-up is coming

title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
pros: Turn-based combat with real-time dodges and parries
Belle Epoque art direction unlike anything else on PC
Story and soundtrack land every emotional swing
cons: No co-op or multiplayer at all
Parry timing walls some players in the first act
Side content thins out badly in the last third

title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
pros: The most convincing medieval world ever built in a game
Every quest has several genuinely different solutions
Fixes almost every complaint about the first game
cons: Systems-heavy opening hours are slow going
Combat stays deliberately awkward against groups
Full price and rarely discounted

title: Split Fiction

displayInfo.players: Exactly 2 (split-screen or online), Friend's Pass for one buyer

pros: Only one of you has to buy it — the other plays free
Swaps genre every 20 minutes and never repeats an idea
Sci-fi and fantasy worlds are both fully realised
cons: Completely unplayable solo
Needs a partner who will finish all 14 hours
Checkpoints can force replaying long set-pieces

title: Elden Ring Nightreign
pros: Elden Ring combat compressed into 40-minute runs
Eight Nightfarers play very differently from each other
Cheaper than a full FromSoftware release
cons: No two-player mode — it is solo or a full trio
Reuses a lot of Elden Ring assets and bosses
Solo runs are markedly harder than balanced

title: Schedule I
pros: Empire-building loop is genuinely hard to put down
Co-op turns logistics into a comedy of errors
Cheap, and one developer keeps shipping updates
cons: Early Access — systems still change between patches
Late game becomes spreadsheet management
Thin story and very rough visuals

title: R.E.P.O.
pros: Physics-based hauling makes every job a disaster
Proximity voice chat does most of the comedy for you
Under S$10 for a whole group-night game
cons: Early Access with a small content pool
Almost pointless alone
Physics jank can wipe a run unfairly

title: Sid Meier's Civilization VII
pros: Three-age structure stops runaway snowballing
Best-looking and best-explained Civ for newcomers
Cross-platform multiplayer with console players
cons: Mixed reviews — long-time fans dislike the age resets
Launched short on UI and diplomacy features
The most expensive game in this catalog

title: Indiana Jones and the Great Circle
pros: First-person adventuring nails the films tonally
Puzzles and hub areas reward genuine exploration
Troy Baker is uncanny as Indy
cons: Full price with no co-op or replay hook
Combat is deliberately clumsy and stays that way
Ray-tracing requirement locks out older GPUs

title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl
pros: The Zone is oppressive, hostile and utterly convincing
Gunplay and survival pressure both hit hard
Enormous open world with no loading seams
cons: Still patching bugs long after launch
Punishing economy and weapon durability
Heavy on VRAM even after optimisation passes

title: Metaphor: ReFantazio
pros: Persona's calendar systems moved into high fantasy
Archetype class system is deep and flexible
75 hours of content for one purchase
cons: Enormous time commitment before it opens up
Dungeon design is weaker than the social half
No co-op, no post-game multiplayer

title: Nine Sols
pros: Sekiro-style parrying in a 2D metroidvania
Taopunk art direction is stunning throughout
Boss fights are the best in the genre
cons: Deflect-or-die combat is unforgiving
Limited accessibility options for the hardest fights
Backtracking between areas gets tedious

title: Ghost of Tsushima Director's Cut
pros: One of the best-looking open worlds on PC
Legends co-op mode is a full second game
Excellent PC port with uncapped frame rates
cons: Open-world checklist structure is very familiar
Requires a PSN account link
Full price, rarely discounted deeply

title: God of War Ragnarok
pros: Combat and weapon variety improve on the 2018 game
Kratos and Atreus carry a genuinely strong script
Runs well across a wide range of hardware
cons: Sequel — start with the 2018 game first
Long stretches of slow walk-and-talk pacing
No co-op or replayable modes

title: Core Keeper
pros: Terraria-style mining and building underground
Scales well from solo to a full group of 8
Cheap for the amount of content
cons: Top-down pixel art will not appeal to everyone
Mid-game grind before the good gear arrives
Thin story and world-building

title: Supermarket Simulator
pros: Restock-price-scan loop is oddly hypnotic
Store expansion gives steady, visible progress
Runs on nearly any laptop
cons: Repetitive once the store is fully upgraded
No combat, story or real challenge
Shoplifter and staff AI is basic

title: Tekken 8
pros: The most aggressive, best-looking Tekken yet
Rollback netcode makes online matches playable from SG
Deep single-player practice and arcade modes
cons: Mixed reviews — heavy microtransactions after launch
Steep execution barrier for new players
Battle pass content behind a full-price game

title: Marvel's Spider-Man 2
pros: Web-swinging and wing-gliding across New York is unmatched
Two playable Spider-Men with distinct movesets
Symbiote combat set-pieces are spectacular
cons: Rough PC port at launch — patched but still heavy
Requires a PSN account link
Short for the asking price with no co-op

title: The Last of Us Part I
pros: Still one of the best-written stories in the medium
Remake visuals and animation are class-leading
Extensive accessibility options
cons: Notorious launch port issues — long shader compiles
Short and near-zero replay value
Expensive for a decade-old game

title: Street Fighter 6
pros: Modern controls make it the friendliest fighter to start
World Tour is a full single-player RPG mode
Best netcode in the genre right now
cons: DLC characters add up well past the base price
Ranked can be brutal without lab time
World Tour visuals are much rougher than versus

title: Against the Storm
pros: Roguelite runs fix the city-builder late-game slump
A settlement takes an hour, not a weekend
Constant meta-progression between runs
cons: No co-op or multiplayer
Timed storms make it stressful, not relaxing
Recipe and resource UI takes hours to read fluently

title: Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader
pros: The first proper CRPG set in Warhammer 40K
Choices genuinely reshape the campaign
Full campaign co-op for up to 6
cons: Buggy at launch and still patch-dependent
Dense 40K jargon assumes some lore knowledge
60 hours is a serious commitment

title: ARK: Survival Ascended
pros: Taming and breeding dinosaurs still has no real rival
Unreal Engine 5 rebuild looks generations newer
Cross-platform official servers stay busy
cons: Mixed reviews — paid remake of a game people owned
Brutal hardware requirements even on low settings
Hundreds of hours of grind by design

title: Warhammer 40,000: Darktide
pros: Melee and gunplay mix better than any other horde shooter
Hive city atmosphere and sound design are superb
Years of free content since a rocky launch
cons: Mostly Positive only — launch damage still shows in reviews
Crafting and progression were reworked repeatedly
Needs a group; random squads fall apart on high difficulty

title: Sifu
pros: Kung fu combat with real weight and readable timing
Ageing mechanic turns death into a running cost
Short enough to actually finish and master
cons: Only 10 hours if you stop at one clear
Difficulty spikes hard at the third boss
No co-op or versus mode

title: Stray
pros: Playing an actual cat is executed perfectly
Neon cyber-city is dense and beautiful
Six hours with no filler at all
cons: Very short for the price
Puzzles are simple throughout
Almost no replay value

title: Grounded
pros: Shrunk-to-ant-size backyard is a brilliant setting
Actually has a story and an ending, unlike most survival games
Arachnophobia slider for the spiders
cons: Full price for a survival game that goes on sale rarely
Base building fights the uneven terrain
Solo play is a big difficulty jump

title: Monster Hunter Rise
pros: Wirebug movement makes it the fastest game in the series
Discounts hard and often — the cheapest way in
Hunts are short enough for a weeknight
cons: Smaller and simpler maps than World or Wilds
Endgame is pure gear grinding
Sunbreak expansion is a separate purchase

title: Inscryption
pros: Goes somewhere no other card game has gone
Escape-room layer around the deckbuilding
Genuinely unsettling without cheap jump scares
cons: The surprise only works once — low replay value
Later acts divide players sharply
Card balance is loose by design

title: Dyson Sphere Program
pros: Factorio in space, across whole star systems
Interstellar logistics scale beyond any single planet
One of the best $/hour ratios in this catalog
cons: Early Access — combat was bolted on late
No co-op or multiplayer
Late-game factories will tax any CPU

title: Forza Horizon 5
pros: Best-feeling arcade driving on PC, pad or wheel
Mexico map is enormous and beautiful
Hundreds of cars included, no grind wall
cons: Requires an Xbox account link
Progression showers you with rewards until they mean nothing
Large install and full price outside sales

title: Crusader Kings III
pros: A story generator disguised as a strategy game
Far friendlier than any previous Paradox title
Every dynasty run goes somewhere different
cons: DLC costs several times the base game
Wars and army management are the weakest part
Runs long — a campaign is dozens of hours

title: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
pros: The most beautiful 2D platformer on PC
Movement feels superb once abilities stack up
Score is worth the price on its own
cons: Escape sequences are stressful and unforgiving
Twelve hours with limited replay value
Requires an Xbox account link

title: Control Ultimate Edition
pros: Telekinetic combat and destructible offices never get old
The Oldest House is one of gaming's great settings
Ultimate Edition includes both expansions
cons: Map and fast travel are genuinely confusing
Difficulty spikes with no options to lower it
Story leaves plenty deliberately unexplained

title: Oxygen Not Included
pros: Thermodynamics simulation nothing else matches
Every failure teaches you exactly what you got wrong
Cheap, and hundreds of hours deep
cons: Brutally unforgiving learning curve
No co-op
Late-game colonies slow down badly

title: Divinity: Original Sin 2
pros: The blueprint that led to Baldur's Gate 3
Elemental combat lets you break every encounter
Four-player co-op with genuinely conflicting goals
cons: Act 2 difficulty spike stops many first runs
Inventory and crafting UI is dated
Sixty hours before credits roll

title: Cuphead
pros: Hand-inked 1930s animation, frame by frame
Boss patterns are hard but always fair
Local co-op doubles the chaos
cons: Co-op is couch only — no online
Genuinely difficult with no easy mode for bosses
Twelve hours if you are good at it

title: XCOM 2
pros: Squad losses hurt because the soldiers are yours
Guerrilla framing beats the original's defensive war
Enormous mod scene, including full conversions
cons: Save-scumming is hard to resist
Performance and load times are dated
War of the Chosen expansion is a separate buy

title: Human Fall Flat
pros: Floppy physics make every solution funny
Free level updates for years after launch
Discounts to a few dollars regularly
cons: Deliberately awkward controls frustrate some players
Puzzles are simple once you stop laughing
Solo play misses the entire point

title: No Man's Sky
pros: Nine years of free updates rebuilt it completely
Seamless planet-to-space flight, no loading screens
Base building, freighters, VR and co-op all included
cons: Procedural planets get samey after a while
Inventory management is still fiddly
The infamous launch reputation still lingers

title: BeamNG.drive
pros: Soft-body crash physics nothing else comes close to
Enormous free mod library of cars and maps
Twelve years of updates and still Early Access-priced
cons: Still officially Early Access after a decade
No official multiplayer
Demanding on CPU with many vehicles
